data.title: How to read this board
data.body:
Each row below is one direction. Left: the popover in a code chat (ENG-6524, PR #236). Right: the same button in an assistant thread.
Blue numbered callouts in both images match the key between them, which ends with pros and cons.
Start with the comparison and Eva's pick up here.

data.title: Context popover for Relay
data.body: A new button left of the panel toggle opens a small popover that changes with what is open. In a code chat: worktree, branch, PR checks and reviews, ledger stage, diff, quick actions. In an assistant thread: what Nova or Astra is doing now, what waits on Isaac, PRs it babysits, experiments. Plus global jobs and Test Bench runs.

data.title: Eva suggests: D, with B's sections
data.body: Pins on top follow Isaac into every chat. Below them, use B's Running, Needs you and Recently done in threads, and A's compact rows in code chats. The labelled button (#236, 3 running) shows the top state without opening the popover.

data.title: Compare the four
data.body:
Direction: shows PRs / shows assistant work / build effort / best for
A Context menu: one status row per fact / one-line rows / low / quick facts and actions
B Now: footer only / running, needs you, done, with progress / medium / threads and global status
C PR card: full card with reviews, checks, ledger / PR list plus today's activity / medium-high / the PR review loop
D Pinned + live: pinned and live rows / live rows plus pins / high (pin store) / a glance across contexts

data.title: Button and placement
data.body: 28px ghost ActionIcon (eva-header-btn) in MainHeader, just left of panel-toggle. Icon follows context: IconGitBranch or IconGitPullRequest in code chats, IconActivity in threads. A 6px dot carries the top state: yellow needs you, blue running, red failing checks, none when idle. Mantine Popover bottom-end, 330 to 380px wide, tooltip on the button.

data.title: Where each context reads from
data.body: Code chat: the chat's worktree (git branch, upstream, dirty, diff --shortstat vs base), work/items/<KEY>.md (stage, move, next, pr), gh pr view (reviews, checks, comments), astra-auto-work job.log (phase). Thread: the session's subagent .jsonl/.md, items with move: isaac, auto-work PRs, work/experiments/*/status.json. Global: jobs/.runs/*.lock and scheduler.log, running Test Bench status.json.

data.title: A · Context menu
data.body: Compact one-line rows like the reference; the skeleton stays, the rows swap per context.

data.title: A · Key
data.body:
1 · New button: icon follows context, the dot shows the top state
2 · Where you are: machine, worktree, Zed, branch (thread: assistant and model)
3 · In flight: PR review, checks, comments, ledger (thread: running subagent, watched PRs)
4 · Next step: Commit & push and the diff (thread: what waits on you)
5 · Global status: running jobs and the Test Bench run, same everywhere

Pros
Fastest to scan, closest to the reference.
Cheapest to build: one Mantine Menu with sections.

Cons
No room for progress or reasons.
Long lists hide behind chevrons.

data.title: B · Now
data.body: Sections for Running, Needs you and Recently done, with progress and a This chat / Everywhere switch.

data.title: B · Key
data.body:
1 · New button: the dot turns blue while something runs
2 · Scope switch: this chat or thread, or Everywhere (global status)
3 · Running, with progress from subagents and experiments
4 · Needs you, with the action inline (Read draft, Review)
5 · Recently done, with times
6 · Footer: branch, PR, diff (thread: jobs and Test Bench)

Pros
Answers what is happening and what needs me at a glance.
Everywhere doubles as the global status view.

Cons
Code facts (branch, Zed, commit) shrink to a footer.
Agents must report progress counts (6 of 10 is illustrative).

data.title: C · PR card
data.body: A rich PR card in code chats; assistant threads fall back to their PR list and today's activity.

data.title: C · Key
data.body:
1 · New button: PR icon in code chats, activity icon in threads
2 · Header: PR title, branch into base, review and ready state (thread: summary and running subagent)
3 · Reviews and checks, per person and per check (thread: PRs it watches)
4 · Ledger stage from the work item (thread: today's auto-work activity)
5 · Diff and actions: Open PR, comments, Open in Zed (thread: Agent Inbox, Jobs)

Pros
Richest view of the PR loop; one click to the PR.
Reads like a PR status page without leaving the chat.

Cons
Tallest of the four and overlaps GitHub.
Chats without a PR need a third layout.

data.title: D · Pinned + live
data.body: Pins Isaac chooses stay on top everywhere; the live context sits below. The button shows a label.

data.title: D · Key
data.body:
1 · Labelled button: the headline (#236, 3 running) plus the state dot
2 · Pinned: Isaac's picks, the same list in every context
3 · Live: this chat's facts (thread: the assistant's running work and asks)
4 · Hover any live row to pin it
5 · Quick actions (thread: global footer)

Pros
One glance across contexts at what Isaac cares about.
The live part still adapts to the chat or thread.

Cons
Pins need upkeep and go stale (#233 is days old).
The labelled button takes header width.
